# Creative Direction Translation Gate

**Sprint:** P0.JURNL.F09-SAFE-TO-SPEND.CREATIVE-DIRECTION-BRAND-EXPRESSION-CORRECTION1
**Source of truth:** `shared/studioos-visual-authority/creative-direction.ts`. `CREATIVE_DIRECTION_GATE.json` is generated by `npx tsx scripts/studioos/visual-authority-export.ts`.

> **A STRONG FUNCTIONAL CONCEPT IS NOT YET A VISUAL AUTHORITY. IMAGE GENERATION IS A RENDERER, NOT THE DESIGNER.**

## Why it exists

JURNL F09 territory proof 1 produced three structurally valid, distinct territories. They passed the blur test and had zero legacy leak. They still read as **good product concepts + clean UI studies**, not creative-directed brand authorities:
- thin environment
- thin materiality
- no graphic-design authorship
- an underused logo
- local HTML renders instead of the image-generation workflow

The pipeline jumped from structure straight to references. This gate is the missing layer.

## Where it sits

```
BRAND DNA → EXPERIENCE CONTRACT → FAMILY CONTRACT → STRUCTURAL TERRITORIES
→ CREATIVE DIRECTION TRANSLATION   (04A · CREATIVE_DIRECTION_READY)
→ BRAND EXPRESSION GATE            (04B · BRAND_EXPRESSION_READY)
→ IMAGE-GENERATED AUTHORITY CANDIDATES (05 · REFERENCE_AUTHORITY_READY)
→ FOUNDER REVIEW → FAMILY AUTHORITY LOCK → RESPONSIVE / STATE EXPLOSION → IMPLEMENTATION
```

## Four layers, kept apart

| Layer | Artifact | Readiness |
|---|---|---|
| STRUCTURAL TERRITORY | `CompositionTerritory`: what the page *is* | `checkTerritoryDistinctness` |
| CREATIVE DIRECTION | `CreativeDirectionTranslation`: how the territory becomes *this brand* | `checkCreativeDirection` → CREATIVE_DIRECTION_READY |
| BRAND EXPRESSION | `BrandExpressionCheck`: proof the whole brand is carried, not palette + font | `checkBrandExpression` → BRAND_EXPRESSION_READY |
| REFERENCE AUTHORITY | `GeneratedCandidate` + `AntiAiAudit` | `checkCandidateAuthority` → REFERENCE_AUTHORITY_READY |

## Project-specific, never universal

Every project supplies its own `CreativeDirectionProfile`. A profile fails if its id is generic, universal or default, or if it belongs to another project. The profile covers:
- brand lines and product philosophy
- logo system (marks, lockups, placement rules, forbidden forms, official assets)
- tagline system
- colour, material, environment and object worlds
- typography direction
- graphic-design rules
- what *wit* means for this brand
- must-not-become list
- anti-generic and anti-AI rules
- renderer: model, quality, aspect, auto-enhance, viewport mapping, generation mode, forbidden providers; local renders are never final

| Project | Profile |
|---|---|
| JURNL | **READY**: `projects/jurnl/creative-direction-profile.ts` |
| AIO · SITE 00 · FRONTAL SLAYER · ASTRAL WORLD · NDXBOOK | **REQUIRED**: each needs its own (see `CREATIVE_DIRECTION_PROJECT_COVERAGE`) |

## The translation

Carried unchanged from the territory:
- structural premise
- primary object (the gate fails if it changes)
- functional metaphor

Required on top of that:
- **22 fields:**
  - art-direction premise
  - brand-world translation
  - graphic-design language
  - environmental role
  - material language
  - tactile object language
  - typographic art direction
  - logo behaviour
  - brand-lockup behaviour
  - colour hierarchy
  - lighting direction
  - depth model
  - compositional tension
  - negative-space strategy
  - editorial wit
  - custom-designed element
  - bespoke detail
  - imagery role
  - focal priority
  - motion implication
  - anti-generic rules
  - anti-AI-look rules
- **`bespoke_visual_idea`:** the one visual idea a generic UI generator could not have produced, recorded verbatim.
- **`render_brief`:** a plain-language description of the finished image, read first by the renderer.
- **≥ 4 graphic-design authorship devices.** The options include:
  - bespoke typographic relationship
  - editorial scale contrast
  - custom material information object
  - designed physical metaphor
  - intentional grid break
  - bespoke labels / tabs
  - tactile data encoding
  - layered physical / graphic structure
  - asymmetric branded framing
  - environment–interface tension
  - custom state transition

  The rule: never simply place UI cards over an image.
- **12 locks, set before any generation call:**
  - primary object
  - major zones
  - visual hierarchy
  - text hierarchy
  - logo placement
  - bottom-nav placement
  - CTA placement
  - image focal points
  - material hierarchy
  - negative-space regions
  - environmental geometry
  - custom object logic
- **Text and prompt:**
  - text that must render (exact)
  - text that may be representational
  - forbidden elements
  - the prompt path (the prompt is built from the locks)

## Creative distinctness

Territories must differ artistically, not only structurally. Every pair must differ on **≥ 8 of 10** dimensions:
- art-direction premise
- environmental strategy
- material strategy
- object language
- typographic strategy
- depth model
- brand-lockup strategy
- visual wit
- data encoding
- CTA expression

Art-direction premise, depth model and material strategy must always differ. Otherwise the result is `CREATIVE_DIRECTION_COLLAPSE`.

**Wit** means a smart visual idea, a meaningful metaphor, a subtle relationship, or a composition that rewards attention. It never means jokes, cute copy or novelty UI.

## Gate integration

`evaluateAuthorityGate` checks this layer for every material family **except** the explicitly grandfathered list (`CREATIVE_DIRECTION_GRANDFATHERED`). Today that list holds only AIO IFTA, whose authority bundle was founder-approved and locked before this gate existed.

- `CREATIVE_DIRECTION_REQUIRED` stops the line before references.
- `BRAND_EXPRESSION_REQUIRED` also stops the line before references.
- References count only when every territory is `REFERENCE_AUTHORITY_READY` and the creative directions are distinct.

The two new guards are `CREATIVE_DIRECTION_REQUIRED` and `BRAND_EXPRESSION_REQUIRED`. See also [BRAND_EXPRESSION_GATE.md](BRAND_EXPRESSION_GATE.md).
